messages:
Aisha (CSM): Quick sync — Hydra is ready for dedicated bring-up next Tues. Need final quota + autoscale plan from SREs. Can folks confirm steady QPS target and burst window? :calendar:
Luca (SRE): Target steady-state 120 qps (95th token latency target <120ms). Burst window planned 10m at 800 qps for warmup.
Priya (Solutions): Customer expects a soft-spot test at 2x predicted peak after warmup. Also asked for an A/B fallback model (smaller quantized) if latency >200ms.
Erin (Customer): Confirmed. Also: legal needs confirmation KMS is in place before go-live for data isolation.
Aisha (CSM): Noted KMS. @Luca can you verify KMS integration and any extra lead time?
Luca (SRE): KMS: we have a customer key in staging, need to rotate to prod key. Ops runbook: restart pool with key env var. Estimated 2h maintenance window.
Priya (Solutions): For autoscale policy, proposing: min_replicas=4, max_replicas=40, scale_up_threshold=70% GPU util over 30s, cool_down=45s. This balances cost and headroom. Thoughts?
Luca (SRE): Agree but suggest scale_up_threshold=65% and use request-based metric (requests/sec per replica) + GPU util to avoid noisy spikes. Also enable warm pool of 2 hot replicas for immediate headroom.
Aisha (CSM): OK that sounds good. Who will run the load test and share results?
Priya (Solutions): Solutions will run initial shadow load in staging. We'll execute two phases: 1) soak at 120 qps for 30m and measure latency/cost; 2) burst script 800 qps for 10m, then 1600 qps short spike for circuit testing.
Luca (SRE): I'll provision the reserved pool and set autoscale rules. I'll also add a guard: fallback_policy -> switch to quantized-model-v1 if P95 latency >200ms for 2 consecutive minutes.
Aisha (CSM): Erin — can you confirm blackout windows for your users? We should avoid your business hour of 9–11am PT.
Erin (Customer): 9–11am PT is live support, avoid. After 6pm works for us.
Aisha (CSM): Scheduling load tests for Tues 18:30 PT then. Plan: warmup, soak, burst, recovery. Priya to post load scripts and expected metrics.
Priya (Solutions): Posting scripts here: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/hydra-loads. Example k6 snippet:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m loadplan.js
```
Expectations: p50 <60ms, p95 <120ms, error-rate <0.1% during soak.
Luca (SRE): devops-bot will kick-off canary before full test. devops-bot: please run health checks and notify on any >5% error spikes.
devops-bot: [automated] Canary deploy started. Health-checks: ok -> 15/15, TTL 2m.
Priya (Solutions): Also capture token-level costs during tests: please export token traces and cost-per-token to the console for postmortem.
Aisha (CSM): Renewal risk note: Erin mentioned potential budget review in 6 weeks. Success criteria for renewal: sustained latency under targets for 2 weeks post-go-live and cost per 1k tokens within quoted range. I'll capture this in the account playbook.
Erin (Customer): Sounds fair. We'll have finance on standby for the review.
Luca (SRE): Action items: (1) provision pool & KMS rotate ticket (ETA Mon AM); (2) apply autoscale policy and warm pool; (3) run canary + assist load test Tue 18:30 PT.
Priya (Solutions): I'll post step-by-step runbook and the k6 Jenkins job.
Aisha (CSM): Great — tagging follow-ups: @Luca please create the provisioning ticket; @Priya paste load job link; @Erin confirm post-test acceptance. :thumbsup:
Erin (Customer): Confirmed — will sign off after review. Thanks everyone.
Aisha (CSM): Closing thread with checklist: provisioning ticket, KMS rotate, autoscale applied, scripts posted, runbook signed, postmortem scheduled. Ping me if anything slips. :lock:
